rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms (ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide coordinated pricing algorithms to Berkeley landlords, and to use them to set rents on residential dwelling units. A coordinated pricing algorithm is a process that uses nonpublic Competitor Data to recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms for future leases, in coordination between a landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor. The ordinance does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge. A secondary source describes recurring unit-per-month violations and private remedies.
rules.key_value: Competitor Data = nonpublic rent, occupancy and lease-date data on other landlords' properties that is less than 90 days old; no penalty amount stated in the passages

coverage.summary: Applies to sellers and users of coordinated pricing algorithms for City of Berkeley residential rental units.

rules.exemptions: Definition excludes (a) products that only publish aggregated, anonymous rental data reports without recommending rents or terms; (b) products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; (c) use of information for market research for project financing, appraisal, or research, testing or training for software development (provided the data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated).
rules.effective_date_note: The only effective date in the passages is a secondary source's 'effective January 2026'. The ordinance's own effective-date clause is not in the retrieved passages.
rules.quoted_span: this ordinance prohibits the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms for the purpose of setting rents on residential dwelling units in the city of Berkeley
rules.review_note: Verify the effective date against the ordinance text. The passages give only the secondary source's January 2026, and the organizer notes a possible conflict with a March 1, 2026 date in the ordinance. Status is treated as in force as of 2026-10-01.
rules.source_notes: Secondary source DX06 (law-firm alert) says ch. 13.63 is effective January 2026 and that RealPage v. City of Berkeley was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice.
